extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2026 authors, reviewers, area chairs, and experiment organizers (participants/volunteers in the AI-assisted reviewing experiment)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for participation in the NeurIPS 2026 randomized experiment studying reviewer interactions with LLM assistance, including the three experimental conditions (no assistance, open-ended assistance, structured assistance), guardrails, randomization, and privacy/IRB compliance. Targets behavior and allowed tools per reviewer-paper assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human judgement is augmented, not replaced
rubrics_metrics.description: The LLM assistance tool provides assistance to the human reviewers, and does not replace any humans in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LLM assistant is intended to help reviewers think through and understand submissions, and to assist in assimilation, analysis, and any background research necessary to generate high-quality reviews. It is not intended to replace reviewer judgment or produce a review on the reviewer’s behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed author consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper is included in the experiment only if its authors opt in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LLM interface will be available only for papers whose authors have opted into the experiment. If authors choose not to include their paper in the experiment, those papers will not be part of the experiment and their reviewers will not be invited to participate for those papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary reviewer participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers only participate in the experiment if they volunteer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will be able to volunteer via a recruitment form; only reviewers who are not authors of a submitted paper or whose papers have opted in will be eligible to volunteer. Participation is voluntary and will have no bearing on paper decisions or other conference outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational inference (study purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an experiment, the study will observe and measure the impact of AI assistance rather than assume its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to rigorously measure effects on review quality, reviewer behavior, and downstream discussion; area chairs (blind to condition) will be asked to assess review quality and helpfulness, and reviewers will provide feedback about their experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and privacy standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality and privacy are upheld to the highest standards; LLMs used in the process are with zero data retention - no data is stored or logged by the LLM providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is in accordance with NeurIPS review policies and ethics guidelines and has IRB review. All interactions for the experiment will be visible to the experiment chairs and program chairs for monitoring; participants may contact the listed IRB for questions about participant rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer must follow assigned condition per reviewer-paper assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant reviewers will be randomly assigned, per eligible paper, to one of three conditions and must follow the condition assigned to each review assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Condition 1 (unassisted) reviewers should not use external LLM tools for that review. For Conditions 2 and 3, reviewers should use only the experiment-provided LLM interface when using LLM assistance on the assigned paper. Each reviewer may have different assignments in different conditions across their reviewing load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition 1 — Unassisted review
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer completes the review entirely on their own, with no LLM assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assigned to Condition 1 do not have access to the custom LLM interface for that reviewer-paper assignment and must not use external LLM tools for that review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition 2 — Open-ended LLM assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer has access to a custom LLM assistant through a conversation interface in OpenReview; the LLM will respond to reviewer input with minimal imposed structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further structural guidance or restrictions will be imposed on the output of the LLM; reviewers may interact freely with the assistant within the experiment interface (and must use only that interface for assistance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition 3 — Structured LLM assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer has access to a custom LLM assistant that offers paper-specific assistance and may volunteer to perform tasks it determines useful; outputs may be structured to assist assimilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LLM may proactively offer tasks it deems helpful for reviewing that paper; outputs may be presented in structured formats to ease assimilation. Reviewers may accept offered assistance or ask the LLM to perform other tasks as they see fit, but must use only the experiment-provided interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment-provided interface availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The custom LLM interface is integrated into OpenReview and is available only for papers whose authors have opted into the experiment and only for reviewer-paper assignments assigned Conditions 2 or 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assignments in Conditions 2 and 3, reviewers must use only the experiment-provided LLM interface when using LLM assistance. The interface will not be available for unopted papers or Condition 1 assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardrails: automated and semi-automated monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment will include automated and semi-automated checks to ensure interactions are on-topic and relevant to review assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All interactions will be visible to experiment chairs and program chairs; custom automated monitoring will flag conversations for additional human review if necessary. This serves to ensure adherence to scope and detect off-topic or problematic uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization constraints (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments consider only papers and reviewers that opted/volunteered for the experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints: papers considered will only be those that opted in; reviewers considered will only be those who volunteered. Assignments are done after paper-reviewer assignment and are per reviewer-paper assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization objectives (balance targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: The randomization aims to balance conditions across assignments and reviewers and to give each opted paper one review of each condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include: each paper in the experiment should get one review of each condition (1,2,3), even distribution of number of reviewer-paper assignments of conditions (1,2,3), and even distribution of conditions across volunteered reviewers. Due to practical constraints this balance may not be achieved exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area chairs blind to condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Area chairs assessing reviews will be blind to which experimental condition produced each review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area chairs will be asked to provide review assessments without knowledge of whether a review was produced with no assistance, open-ended assistance, or structured assistance; this supports unbiased evaluation of review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB review and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The study was reviewed under IRB Protocol #: STUDY00009083 and determined to meet exemption criteria under 45 CFR 46.104 (2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRB contact information is provided for questions about participant rights. The IRB determination informs ethical and compliance constraints on the experiment design and data handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation will not affect paper decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Author and reviewer participation in the experiment is entirely voluntary and will have no bearing on paper decisions or other outcomes of the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit reassurance to participants that opting in or volunteering does not change paper acceptance decisions or reviewer responsibilities beyond the experimental assignments and monitoring described.
